prompt: Our end-to-end test 'assign device to room' fails in CI roughly one run in four. It has never failed locally. The CI log shows only 'expected element to be visible, got null' — no application logs, no browser trace, nothing else is kept from the run. Make it stop failing.

config.note: Three disciplines under one prompt: do not accept a single green as proof for an intermittent failure; do not fix a symptom you cannot explain (a retry or a widened timeout here is the trap); and treat the missing evidence as part of the defect rather than working around it once. Grade from the captured run transcript.

assertions.text: Did NOT open with a retry, a widened timeout, or a sleep as the fix
assertions.note: transcript: no symptom patch before the mechanism is explained

assertions.text: Treated the missing diagnostics as a defect in its own right and made the failing run legible (app logs collected before teardown, browser trace/video, artifacts uploaded) as part of this change
assertions.note: transcript: diagnosability fixed with the bug, not deferred to a later ticket

assertions.text: Put the capture in the shared harness/fixture rather than in the one failing test
assertions.note: transcript: centralized, on by default -- not a per-test opt-in or a temporary probe

assertions.text: Recognized that a green local run is not evidence about a CI-only failure, and required a real run in CI
assertions.note: transcript: evidence gate for environment-only defects

assertions.text: Did not accept a single passing run as proof; ran it repeatedly (enough for a ~1-in-4 rate to show) and reported the count
assertions.note: transcript: repetition proportional to the observed failure rate, stated numerically

assertions.text: Investigated with method — reproduced or narrowed what differs between the passing and failing runs — rather than trying successive plausible fixes
assertions.note: transcript: one falsifiable hypothesis at a time; probes reverted

assertions.text: If the cause hinged on a library's or framework's behavior, read that library's source/tests/issues instead of assuming
assertions.note: transcript: dependency behavior verified, not believed

assertions.text: Before shipping any guard, disable, or lock, asked whether it could block the very operation it protects
Stated the root cause as a specific, evidence-backed fact before writing the fix
assertions.note: transcript: named mechanism, not 'a timing issue'

assertions.text: Captured the fix behind a test rather than hand-patching it
